summary: Nobumi Iyanaga is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1968–1969). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003) and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (2008–2014).

Nobumichi Kusumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.
Nobuo Otsuka is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University (~1983–1988) and later served as a researcher there (attested 1995).

Nobuyoshi Yamabe, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at Osaka, Otani, and Yale universities under mentors including Noritoshi Aramaki and Stanley Weinstein. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Agriculture (2003) and Waseda University (2015).

Nobuyuki Kaji is a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Kyoto and Tohoku universities. He served as professor at Osaka University (1984–1998), president of Koshien Junior College (1998–1999), and special invited professor at Ritsumeikan University (2008–2015).

Nobuyuki Watase is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his master's degree at Kyoto University (~1963–1966). He served as professor at Tokai University (~1984–2007) and president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2010).

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (~1959–1968) under Genjun Sasaki and Issai Funahashi. He served as a lecturer and research appointee at Otani University between ~1981 and ~2011.

Nora Kershaw Chadwick was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Newnham College (~1911–1914). She held academic posts at the University of St Andrews (~1919–1923) and the University of Cambridge (~1950–1958).

Norbert Max Samuelson was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. He held major posts at Temple University (1975–1998) and Arizona State University (~1998–2018).

Noriaki Hakamaya is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Shun'ei Hirai and Zuiho Yamaguchi, he was a professor at Komazawa University from 1985 to 2011.
Noriaki Hosoda is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who served at Hokkaido University as a research assistant (attested 1986) and associate professor (attested 2003).
Noriaki Inoue is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953) and later served as a professor there (attested 1982).

Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku, Bukkyo, and Visva-Bharati universities. He spent his career at Bukkyo University, serving as professor from 1994 and becoming professor emeritus in 2015.
Norihiko Uchida is a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied under Yutaka Ochihara and served as an assistant at the Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1962).

Norihisa Baba is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda. He joined Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, becoming a full professor in 2019.
Norio Koyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 2014).

Noritoshi Aramaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his doctorate at Kyoto University. He held professorships at Osaka University (~1981–1991), Kyoto University (~1991–2000), and Otani University (~2000–2005).

Noriyuki Kudo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed postgraduate studies at Bukkyo University. He served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University and as an associate professor at Soka University (attested 2000–2013).

Norman Fischer is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Colgate, the University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union. He studied under traditional teachers Sojun Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker, founding the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.
Norvin J. Hein was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion at Yale Divinity School (attested 1965).
